newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA BIOCHIM BANK REPORTS ZERO 96 NET PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA BIOCHIM BANK REPORTS ZERO 96 NET PROFIT.

text.p: Bulgaria's state-owned Biochim Bank posted zero net profit last year after setting aside 66.5 billion levs for provisions against bad debts, a senior bank official said on Monday.

"The bank has a zero net profit for 1996 after setting aside 66.5 billion levs for provisions against its non-performing loans," Biochim executive director Maria Ivanova told the shareholders meeting.
After adjusting its hard currency assets to the new, weaker lev rate, the bank posted a 66.5 billion levs gross profit, AFA auditing company said in its report.
The lev nose dived from to 600 to the dollar in January and 3,000 in February this year from 70 a year ago.
The auditors said that the bank's income statement and its balance sheet realistically presented the bank's status but they expressed doubts about the future of the institution.
"Unless government and central bank support is accompanied with restructuring of the bank's loan portfolio Biochim Bank's ability to function in the future is doubtful," their report said.
Biochim has a two-year twinning agreement for technical advice with the Dutch ABN Amro Bank signed last year.
Uncovered losses from previous years stood at 2.7 billion levs and the bank's capital-to-risk ratio was negative 27.8 percent at the end of 1996, the bank's balance sheet showed.
In April Bulgaria's finance ministry issued $50 million 18-month T-notes due to be bought out by Bulgaria's biggest bank Bulbank, as part of a Biochim Bank stabilisation plan.

So far the bank has received the first $20 million tranche and was expected to receive the remaining $30 million shortly before the introduction of a restrictive fixed exchange rate regime, known as a currency board.
Last year Biochim suffered serious liquidity problems because of panic withdrawals caused by a chain of bank closures.

At the end of 1996 the credits extended by Biochim to financial institutions, individuals and firms totalled 106.4 billion levs, of which 75.6 percent or 73.2 billion levs were clasified as uncollectable loans.
The bank's total assets amounted to 187 billion levs at the end of 1996.

Biochim has 143.9 billion levs profit for the first quarter of this year and its total assets increased to 495.7 billion levs mainly due to the lev's slump, Biochim Bank's executive director Katia Ivanova told reporters.
Biochim Bank was set up through a merger of former Biochimbank, Sofia Bank and Serdika Bank in August 1995 by the Bank Consolidation Company (BCC).
The BCC, which manages state equity in local commercial banks, holds over 99 percent of Biochim Bank's share capital. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
